name: AT42QT1070 5-pad capacitive touch sensor
description: Microchip/Atmel QTouch capacitive touch controller used in standalone mode: five touch pads (key 0 is a guard key), each with an open-drain output that goes low while its pad is touched; only one key is reported at a time. Runs on 1.8–5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit Standalone 5-Pad Capacitive Touch Sensor Breakout - AT42QT1070 (product #1362), two 6-pin headers (Gnd, Input 0-4 / VDD, Output 0-4), standalone only, no I2C.
eli5: Turns five pieces of copper foil into touch buttons: touch one and its output wire goes low, just like pressing a button to ground.

pins.name: IN0
pins.description: Touch pad 0 electrode input (printed '0' under 'Input'), 10 kOhm series resistor on board; connect a copper pad, not the microcontroller — key 0 is the guard key

pins.name: IN1
pins.description: Touch pad 1 electrode input (printed '1' under 'Input'), 10 kOhm series resistor on board; connect a copper pad, not the microcontroller

pins.name: IN2
pins.description: Touch pad 2 electrode input (printed '2' under 'Input'), 10 kOhm series resistor on board; connect a copper pad, not the microcontroller

pins.name: IN3
pins.description: Touch pad 3 electrode input (printed '3' under 'Input'), 10 kOhm series resistor on board; connect a copper pad, not the microcontroller

pins.name: IN4
pins.description: Touch pad 4 electrode input (printed '4' under 'Input'), 10 kOhm series resistor on board; connect a copper pad, not the microcontroller

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply 1.8–5.5 V (right 'Output' header, top); use 3.3 V with an ESP32 or Pico

pins.name: OUT0
pins.description: Open-drain output, LOW while pad 0 is touched (printed '0' under 'Output'); LED + 470 Ohm to VDD on board but no pull-up

pins.name: OUT1
pins.description: Open-drain output, LOW while pad 1 is touched (printed '1' under 'Output'); LED + 470 Ohm to VDD on board but no pull-up

pins.name: OUT2
pins.description: Open-drain output, LOW while pad 2 is touched (printed '2' under 'Output'); LED + 470 Ohm to VDD on board but no pull-up

pins.name: OUT3
pins.description: Open-drain output, LOW while pad 3 is touched (printed '3' under 'Output'); LED + 470 Ohm to VDD on board but no pull-up

supplierQuery: Adafruit 1362 AT42QT1070 standalone 5-pad capacitive touch breakout
buildNotes: Two 6-pin headers: left 'Input' = Gnd, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (touch pads); right 'Output' = VDD, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (open-drain outputs). Wire it with jumper leads.

Each output goes LOW while its pad is touched. The board only has an LED + 470 Ohm to VDD on each output, no pull-up: fit 10 kOhm to 3.3 V or enable the GPIO's internal pull-up (ESP32 GPIO34-39 have none).
Power VDD from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico; the chip runs on 1.8-5.5 V, but keep the pull-ups' voltage no higher than VDD + 0.5 V.
Pad 0 is the guard key: it has priority and suppresses the other keys, and only one key is reported at a time.
Pads: copper foil or plates at least 6 x 6 mm, short wires. The chip calibrates at power-up, so don't touch the pads while powering on; a touch held for about 30 s is recalibrated away.
This board is standalone only (MODE tied to VDD): it cannot be read over I2C.

example.code:
from qt1070 import QT1070
import time

pad = QT1070([{OUT0}, {OUT1}, {OUT2}, {OUT3}, {OUT4}])
while True:
    print('touched=%s' % pad.touched())
    time.sleep_ms(200)

test.title: Reports pad 2 while it is touched
